title: Prompt references (@@@prompt:...@@@) are only valid in plain-text prompts
answers: Why is a JSON/structured prompt with a @@@prompt tag rejected?
Can I use prompt references inside structured or message-based prompts?
body:
Prompt references (`@@@prompt:name=...|label=...@@@`) may only appear in plain-text (string) prompt payloads. Non-string (JSON) payloads containing a tag are rejected with 400 and code `reference_in_non_text_prompt`.
Enforced in `products/ai_observability/backend/prompt_references.py:validate_reference_targets`, which create, publish and duplicate all share.
Reason: fetch-time splicing inserts raw, unescaped text into the surrounding document, so quotes/newlines in the referenced prompt corrupt JSON.
The check runs on the raw `prompt_payload` (isinstance str), not only on normalized text, and only after the early return when no references are found, so JSON payloads without tags are unaffected.
This mirrors the existing rule that referenced targets must be plain text. Legacy content written before the rule is not rewritten.
applies: LLM prompt management API (create/publish/duplicate) in products/ai_observability and posthog/api llm_prompt
